title: Which AI for 2D graphics?
author: spyromon13
selftext:
Hello guys.

I'm building a small project with Claude and I'm missing 2D dark fantasy graphics/sprites. Which AI do you think is the best to use?

replies.author: spyromon13
replies.body: To what extent can I trust them to maintain the same art style? Also, should I use another tool to add movement, or will they be able to generate the frames for me?

replies.author: Marod_
replies.body: The first thing you should to is try to create a good reference image with as bunch of different types of objects. Then always tell it to use it as the reference. I'm doing 3D but this as worked pretty well for me so far.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/x7s7049m62yh1.png

I've been using GPT Imagegen in combination with a pixel snapping and downscaling workflow. 

I'm happy with the results; dunno if it's to anyone else's tastes. If you think it's interesting I'd be happy to elaborate on the process. 

I'm using imagegen for a very specific reason - it is one of the only image generators that will consistently provide a dynamic-looking pose for a character. All of the other image generators give consistent but stiff-looking and boring poses, IMHO. 

The trade-off is the imagegen is a slop factory and you have to do a lot of clean-up, and even after clean-up you still get a sort of grainy texture on the sprites. I don't mind it, and you could probably solve at least some of it with dithering and/or a noise reduction algo. 

  
If you want much cleaner sprites, Pixel Lab and Sprite Fusion are the places to go. Second to nothing. But they're expensive for what they offer, and  (IMHO) the poses are just very static.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
I started using a new prompt in Gemini if you wanted to try it. I basically make a video and then you can dissect the video frames into sprite sheets. The content (like dark fantasy in your case) isn't relevant since you can use a starter image. I'll make a starter image and depict the progress in this chat to consider its use on your own.

So first generate your basic image and cut it into a png. Not necessary, but it helps the Ai specify a task.

https://i.redd.it/p9oese1vd2yh1.jpeg

replies.author: Entropydemic
replies.body:
Video of the single 2D pixel art character from (CuteDragonGirl.png), maintaining anime cute anatomical proportions, realistic head-to-body ratio, and tall slender fighting game posture from the reference image. The character stays facing the left edge of the frame at all times in the center of the screen, performing a fluid, high-frame-rate martial arts animation sequence with dynamic body mechanics and natural weight transfer:
Action 1: relaxed breathing idle stance, transitioning smoothly into an athletic run-in-place facing left,
Action 2: fluid, full-body forward slashes with her claw hands with natural shoulder and hip follow-through,
Action 3: forward palm strike to the left, lunging slightly into the strike with a bent knee,
Action 4: agile vertical jumping tail strike facing left with bent knees and smooth landing recovery,
Action 5: snappy left-facing tail whip with full hip extension, retracting the leg smoothly back into a left-facing stance without turning around,
Action 6: loses balance and collapses unconscious facing left.
​Visual & Technical Constraints:
High-resolution 2D arcade fighting game pixel art (realistic 8-heads-tall anime proportions, no chibi, no oversized head), orthographic side-view, 16:9 aspect ratio. Smooth, fluid hand-drawn pixel animation with natural joint articulation and momentum. Character is isolated in a void against a completely flat, unlit #00FF00 solid chroma key green background. 100% flat ambient lighting, shadeless, unlit texture, zero cast shadows, zero contact occlusion, no ground plane, no floor, no horizon line, no gradients, no depth. No special effects, no particles, no sound effects, no music.
